canonicalIngredients.name: sausage mince
observations: 500 g, blended with beef for fat/juiciness (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: brown onion
observations: 1 diced in mix + 2 large sliced in gravy (s3)

canonicalIngredients.name: beef stock
observations: 3 cups water + 6 tbsp gravy mix instead (s3)

canonicalIngredients.name: beef stock powder
observations: 2 Oxo cubes or 2 tbsp in mix (s3)

causalSequence: combine mince, onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, worcestershire, seasonings; mix by hand until just combined
portion; shape thick patties with wet hands
brown rissoles in oiled pan over medium heat, in batches, turning once
remove rissoles; soften sliced onion (with butter) in same pan
stir flour into onions; cook 1 min
whisk in beef stock and worcestershire; simmer few min to thicken
return rissoles to gravy; simmer low 8-10 min until gravy thick and glossy
serve with mashed potato and steamed greens
techniqueFacts: batch-fry without crowding so rissoles brown instead of steam (3 sources)
medium heat preserves juiciness; high heat dries the outside before the centre cooks (2 sources)
keep shape thick, not flattened like a burger, to hold juices (2 sources)
don't overwork the mix or rissoles turn firm (2 sources)
finishing rissoles by simmering in the gravy tenderises them and trades flavour both ways (2 sources)
grated onion gives pulp that seasons the mix without chunks (1 source)
sausage mince blended with beef adds fat for tenderness and old-fashioned flavour (1 source)
regular not lean mince is required for juicy rissoles (2 sources)
gravy path splits: scratch roux of butter-flour-beef stock (1 source) vs packet gravy mix in water (1 source) vs deglazed pan drippings (1 source)
stock powder in the mix is a flavour lever interchangeable with salt (2 sources)
